feedback: Written before this robot races. Hold the iteration-2 geometry, as you proposed. Across all eleven raced designs, every run ended off_track with max_error between 0.0604 and 0.0617 m. Span of ±0.05 m is the only change that mattered, because it removed line loss on oval and slalom (iteration 1). Footprint (iterations 1 and 2), kp from 2.6 to 4.4 (iterations 2, 4, 7), wheel_track 0.10, 0.12 and 0.15 m (iterations 4 and 8), mass 0.6 kg (iteration 5), wheel_radius 0.04 m (iteration 7, which scored worse), and sensor y from 0.02 to 0.06 m (iterations 3 and 6; 0.06 m reintroduced line loss) all left max_error at about 0.061 m. Iteration 9 showed kd 0.15 made no difference. The one change that moved the score was base_speed 1.2 (iteration 10, score 27.3854), so speed is the lever to read, not geometry. The package holds the iteration-2 geometry and the iteration-10 controller. Because there is no later iteration, no further geometry test can be run, so the requested changes below are for the record and for any future team.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-2 geometry (16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg). Do not re-test span, footprint, mass, track, radius or y, since each has been tested with no effect on max_error.

If a future team has another iteration, ask the Integrator to report the step or bend at which max_error peaks on each track. A start-up transient and a steady offset need different geometry responses, and the Builder has no other way to tell them apart.
Only propose a geometry change with a named start-up hypothesis and the measurement that would confirm it. Speed (base_speed 1.2 versus 1.6) is the only lever that has moved the score since span.
